title: Optimized Protocol for Fluorescent Lectin/Immunohistochemistry in Human and Rodent Tissues
author: Rebelo, Contessotto, et al.

steps.title: Warm tissue sections for adhesion
steps.instruction: Leave frozen tissue sections on a slide warmer at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C) for 30 min to 1 h to evaporate moisture and improve adhesion. If the tissue was not fixed before freezing, incubate the sections with 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) on the slide for 2 min inside a fume hood.

steps.title: Create hydrophobic barrier
steps.instruction: Draw a circle or frame around each tissue section with a PAP pen to form a hydrophobic barrier that prevents lectin solution leakage. If the barrier disappears during later steps, carefully dry the glass borders near the tissue and redraw the barrier.

steps.title: Wash sections with TBS‑T
steps.instruction: Wash the sections three times, 3 min each, at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C) in a glass Coplin staining jar placed on a shaking platform at low speed (60–80 rpm). Monitor the sections to ensure they do not detach from the slide.

steps.title: Arrange slides in staining system
steps.instruction: Lay the slides horizontally with the tissue side up in an opaque (blackout) StainTray slide‑staining system. If a StainTray is unavailable, place the slides on glass rods inside an opaque sandwich box lined with damp filter paper or a similar alternative.

steps.title: Block with periodate‑treated BSA
steps.instruction: Block sections with 3 % periodate‑treated bovine serum albumin (BSA) in TBS for 1 h at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C). Prepare the blocking solution fresh immediately before use.

steps.title: Wash with TBS
steps.instruction: Wash sections three times, 3 min each, at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C) in TBS with gentle shaking. From this point onward, protect the samples from direct light; perform all remaining steps in darkness or under red light to avoid fluorescence quenching.

steps.title: Incubate with fluorescent lectin
steps.instruction: Incubate sections with fluorescently labelled lectins diluted in TBS‑T for 1 h at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C) in a dark chamber (StainTray or equivalent). Prepare lectin working solutions fresh 30 min before staining and discard after use. Perform a titration experiment beforehand to determine the optimal lectin concentration. For specificity controls, pre‑incubate each lectin with 100 mM appropriate haptenic sugar in TBS‑T for at least 30 min, then add the lectin‑sugar mixture to the tissue; include a positive‑control tissue known to display the target glycan.

substeps.instruction: Titrate lectin concentration on test sections.
Prepare inhibition controls with 100 mM haptenic sugar, pre‑incubate ≥30 min.

steps.title: Wash post‑lectin incubation
steps.instruction: Wash sections twice with TBS‑T, 3 min each, then once with TBS (no detergent) at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C). Perform drop washes while keeping slides horizontal in the StainTray. For brain tissue, wash twice with TBS‑T for 10 min each and twice with TBS for 10 min each to reduce lipid‑derived autofluorescence.

steps.title: Counterstain nuclei
steps.instruction: Counterstain either with Hoechst 33342 diluted 1:2000 (final 0.01 mM) in TBS for 5–10 min at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C), or apply a single drop of ProLong™ Gold Antifade Mountant with DAPI per ≈0.5 cm² tissue section.

steps.title: Wash after Hoechst and optional Sudan black B
steps.instruction: If Hoechst 33342 was used, wash sections three times with TBS, 3 min each, at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C). For brain or other lipofuscin‑rich tissues, after these washes incubate with 0.1 % Sudan black B solution in 70 % ethanol (1 mg mL⁻¹) for 5 min at room temperature, then wash twice with TBS for 4 min each. Sudan black B solution can be reused up to three times.

steps.title: Mount slides
steps.instruction: Apply one or two drops of Fluoromount™ aqueous mounting media and cover the slide with a glass coverslip (one drop is sufficient for ≈0.5 cm²). If ProLong™ Gold Antifade Mountant with DAPI was used previously, this step is unnecessary.

steps.title: Cure slides
steps.instruction: Leave slides to cure overnight (≈16 h) at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C) in the dark, then seal the coverslip edges with clear nail polish to prevent movement and drying of the mountant.

steps.title: Store slides until imaging
steps.instruction: Store slides at 4 °C until imaging. Image within 4 days for best results; precious samples may be stored at –20 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Image stained slides
steps.instruction: Acquire images using a fluorescence microscope; confocal microscopy is recommended to obtain Z‑stacks for higher resolution. Image within 4 days and consult troubleshooting if unexpected outcomes occur.

steps.title: Optional pause after lectin staining
steps.instruction: If immediate immunostaining is not possible, keep lectin‑stained sections overnight covered with TBS in a humidified chamber before proceeding.

steps.title: Second block before antibody (optional)
steps.instruction: Keep slides in the StainTray (or equivalent) and block again with 3 % periodate‑treated BSA in TBS for 1 h at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C). This step is optional and may be omitted depending on the antibody; serum‑based blocking can affect lectin binding and should be evaluated with controls.

steps.title: Incubate primary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate sections with the primary antibody at the previously optimized concentration, time, and temperature (typically overnight ≈16 h at 4 °C or 2 h at room temperature ≈18 °C–23 °C), diluted in either TBS or TBS‑T. Use TBS throughout; do not switch to PBS.

steps.title: Wash after primary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash sections twice with TBS‑T for 10 min each, then once with TBS for 10 min, at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C). Perform drop washes while keeping slides horizontal in the StainTray. For brain or highly autofluorescent tissue, perform vertical washes in a glass Coplin jar.

steps.title: Incubate secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate sections with fluorescently labelled secondary antibody diluted in TBS (optimized dilution) for 1 h at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C). Choose fluorophores that do not spectrally overlap with the lectin label (e.g., if lectin is FITC, avoid Alexa Fluor 532; FITC + Alexa Fluor 647 is acceptable).

steps.title: Wash after secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash sections three times with TBS, 3 min each, at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C) using drop washes in the StainTray. For brain or cardiac tissue, wash once with TBS‑T for 10 min and three times with TBS for 10 min each, using vertical washes in a glass Coplin jar.

steps.title: Counterstain nuclei (antibody)
steps.instruction: Counterstain with Hoechst 33342 diluted 1:2000 (final 0.01 mM) in TBS for 5–10 min at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C), or apply a single drop of ProLong™ Gold Antifade Mountant with DAPI per ≈0.5 cm² tissue section.

steps.title: Wash after Hoechst and optional Sudan black B (antibody)
steps.instruction: If Hoechst 33342 was used, wash three times with TBS, 3 min each at room temperature. For brain or lipofuscin‑rich tissue, after these washes incubate with 0.1 % Sudan black B in 70 % ethanol (1 mg mL⁻¹) for 5 min at room temperature, then wash twice with TBS for 4 min each. Sudan black B solution may be reused up to three times.

steps.title: Mount slides (antibody)
steps.instruction: Apply one or two drops of Fluoromount™ aqueous mounting media and cover with a glass coverslip (single drop sufficient for ≈0.5 cm²). Skip this step if ProLong™ Gold Antifade Mountant with DAPI was used earlier.

steps.title: Cure slides (antibody)
steps.instruction: Allow slides to cure overnight (≈16 h) at room temperature (≈18 °C–23 °C) in the dark, then seal the coverslip edges with clear nail polish.

steps.title: Store slides until imaging (antibody)
steps.instruction: Store slides at 4 °C until imaging. Image within 3 days for optimal results; samples may be stored at –20 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Image stained slides (antibody)
steps.instruction: Acquire images using a fluorescence microscope (confocal recommended for Z‑stacks). Image within 3 days and refer to troubleshooting if needed.
